headline: Sykes survives Humphries fightback to win 10-9
standfirst: Tom Sykes led 4-0, was pegged back to 6-5 down, and still beat Luke Humphries in a deciding leg to reach the Grand Slam of Darts quarter-finals.
body: Tom Sykes knocked out second seed Luke Humphries 10-9 in the last 16 of the Grand Slam of Darts on Thursday night, taking the deciding leg in 13 darts with a 36 checkout. Humphries had the throw in that leg and could not hold.

Sykes, making his debut in the event, was ahead 4-0 after four legs, including an 11-darter in the fourth. Humphries then won the next two and, after Sykes broke back for 5-2, claimed four more legs in a row to take the lead for the first time at 6-5.

Sykes responded. He levelled at 6-6, broke throw with a 114 finish in leg 13 and won the next to lead 8-6. Humphries pulled back to 8-9 with an 87 checkout and then broke with an 81 to make it 9-9, setting up the decider.
Humphries averaged 102.02 to Sykes’s 99.32, but Sykes hit eight 180s to four and converted 43.48 per cent of his finishing chances against 37.5. Sykes made five breaks of throw in all.
He faces Michael van Gerwen in the quarter-finals on Saturday evening.
